summary: Reserved-pool throughput sag and elevated tail latency during multi-tenant burst (GPU bind skew + autoscale undersize)
description: Issue summary: During a customer-triggered burst of inference traffic from EdgeShop's dedicated reservation on prod-us-east we observed a sustained throughput drop and elevated tail latency for ~2 hours. Impact: customer-facing endpoints returned increased p95/p99 latency (p95 from ~220ms to ~1.8s; p99 spikes up to 6s) and intermittent 504 gateway timeouts. Several streaming sessions dropped mid-response. Environment: Dedicated reserved pool (reservation-id: rsv-77a9), prod-us-east, serving-runtime 2.14.1, autoscaler policy 'reserved-default-v2'. Steps to reproduce: 1) Millisecond-scale burst of mixed short & long sequences from ~20 tenants simultaneously hitting the pool (simulated by EdgeShop load test). 2) Observe queue depth and GPU utilization on the pool. 3) Notice per-pod request queues and increasing context-switching on GPU. Observed behavior: Autoscaler did not scale up quickly enough (scale-up step size set to +1 pod per 60s), some pods exhibited GPU-binding skew where NV_link-local bindings caused one GPU to reach >95% active CUDA context while sibling GPU on same node sat at ~40%. This caused head-of-line queueing, frequent preemption of KV cache transfers, and a rise in tail latency and 504s. Expected behavior: Reservation should sustain burst with autoscaler adding capacity before significant tail latency increases; GPU binding should balance across sockets and CUDA contexts to avoid single-GPU hotspots. Initial hypothesis: Combination of autoscale step-size too small for multi-tenant burst and a recent kernel upgrade (serving-runtime 2.14.1) changed CUDA stream scheduling leading to GPU bind skew. Attachments/logs: links to dashboards and flamegraphs below.

investigation_notes: Pulled pod-level GPU metrics from prometheus: nvml_utilization_gpu for node n-prod-12 showed [GPU0: 96%, GPU1: 42%] averaged across affected window.
Servicing logs show repeated context rebinds and increased memcpy from host to device during KV cache warms, correlating with latency spikes.
Autoscaler logs: scale events were rate-limited by default step size and cooldown (60s cooldown). During burst the backlog grew faster than step size could compensate.
Reproduced locally in a staging mirror by replaying EdgeShop trace: enabling balanced-affinity in runtime prevented GPU skew and eliminated the p99 spikes.
Runtime diff between 2.13.x and 2.14.1 includes changed CUDA stream priority handling (PR 4011) which can alter context distribution under multi-tenant loads.
No evidence of hardware alarms or ECC errors. NVidia driver versions consistent across nodes (525.xx).
resolution_notes: Hotfix deployed to impacted region: runtime rollback/patch (serving-runtime 2.14.1 -> 2.14.1+patch1) that forces balanced GPU affinity when reserved pools detect uneven context distribution.
Autoscaler policy for reserved pools updated: increased maximum step size to +3 pods/minute for large reservations and reduced cooldown to 30s when backlog > 250 requests.
Added a protective routing policy: when per-pod GPU imbalance > 25% for >2m, route new short-sequence requests to alternate compatible pool to avoid head-of-line blocking.
Customer (EdgeShop) validated with a 2-hour soak; p95/p99 stayed within expected ranges and 504s ceased.
Linked INT-4120 opened to track a thorough postmortem and a long-term autoscaler redesign.
Communicated RCA and mitigation to customer and internal channels.
workaround: Temporarily increased autoscale step size and enabled GPU-affinity fallback on the reservation; recommended customer to stagger burst windows until autoscaler changes were applied.
follow_up_actions: INT-4120: Conduct full postmortem and timeline; include SLO/alert tuning recommendations.
Autocaler redesign ticket to evaluate predictive scaling based on request queue growth rate and sequence-length mix.
Runtime team to add a regression test in CI that replicates multi-tenant burst with mixed sequence lengths to catch GPU affinity regressions.
Add dashboard alert: 'reserved-pool gpu-imbalance' to trigger before p95 exceeds threshold.
Update customer runbook to include steps to request emergency scaling for large reserved bursts.
